title: Perform Post-slaughter Procedures for Small Stock Carcasses

lessons.title: Following inspection and trimming
lessons.html:
Step 1: Wait for the inspector's decision

After dressing, every carcass with its head and organs is inspected. You must follow the decision every time.

  • Passed: continue to trimming and washing.
  • Trim: remove the parts the inspector shows you.
  • Detained: move the carcass and its organs to the detain rail only when told to. Do not work on it.
  • Condemned: take it to the condemned bin or room. Keep it separate. Never take any part.

Step 2: Final trimming

  1. Use a sharp, sterile knife.
  2. Start at the top of the hanging carcass and work down.
  3. Trim off wool, hair, dirt, dung, bruises and blood clots.
  4. Trim the neck and sticking wound.
  5. Put trimmings in the correct container: edible trimmings separate from condemned material.
  6. Sterilise the knife after each trim of contamination.

Trim only what needs to be removed. Over-trimming loses meat and money for the farmer.

Step 3: Final wash

  1. Wash with clean, potable water from the top down.
  2. Wash off blood and bone dust.
  3. Do not wash wool or dung; trim it.
  4. Do not splash floor water onto the carcass.

lessons.title: Weighing, recording and chilling
lessons.html:
Step 4: Weighing

  1. Check the scale is set to zero, as your plant procedure says.
  2. Let the carcass hang freely on the scale, not touching anything.
  3. Read the mass in kilograms.
  4. Record the carcass number, owner and mass on the kill sheet or computer.
  5. Check that the number on the carcass and the record match.

Step 5: Classification and marking

The trained classifier checks age and fat and marks the carcass with a roller mark. Passed carcasses get the inspection stamp. Only authorised people do this. Make sure the carcass is presented so they can see it clearly.

Step 6: Chilling

  1. Move the carcass into the chiller promptly.
  2. Hang it with space all around; it must not touch other carcasses, walls or the floor.
  3. Close the chiller door each time.
  4. Check and record chiller temperatures as your plant procedure requires.
  5. Report a warm chiller, a broken door seal or water dripping from the ceiling.

Offal

  • Passed red offal is trimmed, rinsed, chilled and packed.
  • Cleaned tripe is chilled separately.
  • Keep edible offal separate from inedible material.

Skins

Skins are taken to the skin store, spread out, and salted or kept as your plant arranges. Keep the skin store away from meat areas.

lessons.title: Dispatch and record-keeping
lessons.html:
Step 7: Preparing for dispatch

  1. Read the order: customer, number of carcasses, class, any offal.
  2. Pick the right carcasses from the chiller. Check numbers and marks.
  3. Check the truck: clean inside, cold, with rails and hooks.
  4. Report a dirty or warm truck; do not load it.

Step 8: Loading

  • Wear clean clothing, a hairnet and clean hands.
  • Hang carcasses on the truck rails. Never put them on the truck floor.
  • Do not let carcasses rub on dirty surfaces.
  • Load quickly and close the truck doors to keep it cold.

Step 9: Documents

  • Complete the dispatch note: date, customer, carcass numbers, total mass.
  • Get it signed by the driver.
  • Keep your copy as your plant procedure says.

Why records matter

If a customer complains or there is a food safety problem, the abattoir must be able to trace every carcass back to the day it was slaughtered and the farm it came from. This is called traceability. It only works if every record is correct.

Safety

  • Lamb carcasses are not very heavy, but carrying many causes back strain. Use the rails.
  • Chiller floors can be slippery. Wear non-slip boots and warm clothing.
  • Know how to open the chiller door from the inside.

Key points

  • Follow every inspection decision: pass, trim, detain or condemn.
  • Trim from top to bottom with a sterile knife; trim only what is needed.
  • Weigh carefully and check that carcass numbers match the record.
  • Chill quickly with space around each carcass and record temperatures.
  • Load only into clean, cold trucks and complete the dispatch note.
  • Correct records make traceability possible.

quiz.question: What should you do with a detained carcass?

options.text: Move it to the detain rail only when told and do not work on it
Send it to the chiller with the others

quiz.question: Where do you start trimming a hanging carcass?

options.text: It loses meat and money for the farmer
Tracing a picture of a sheep
Being able to trace every carcass back to its slaughter day and farm

options.text: Report it and do not load
Put the carcasses on the floor
